thread:
alice: Heads up — I pushed a change to the tf-modules/gpupool module that renames the variable map `kms_settings` -> `kms_config`. It landed on staging/main and now a bunch of GitOps CI plans are failing with missing var errors. Anyone else seeing this?
ben: Yep CI alerted me. Example failure: "The module variable \"kms_settings\" is required but not set" when running plan against several downstream repos.
carmen: That was my change — I renamed for clarity but I didn’t add a backward-compat shim. Sorry, my bad.
dmitri: Can we add a deprecated var and prefer the new one via locals? Something like: ```hcl
variable "kms_settings" { type = map(string) default = {} description = "DEPRECATED - use kms_config" }
locals { kms = length(var.kms_config) > 0 ? var.kms_config : var.kms_settings }
``` Should be non-breaking for consumers that still set kms_settings.
alice: Yep that pattern works. Also add a migration note and bump patch. We need to be careful because many consumers pin module by git ref/sha.
ben: Consumers pinning commits is the messy part. If they point at the commit that removed the var, shim will fix future tags but pinned commits still break CI until they update refs. We should cut a patch release and backport shim to the stable branch.
carmen: I'll open a hotfix PR restoring the deprecated var + locals and add tests. Also adding a CI rule to detect removal/rename of module inputs without a major bump.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Created patch release terraform-aws-gpupool v1.2.5 (draft).
dmitri: For repos that vendor module by commit, we should script a mass-update or at least create a migration job that opens PRs to the top consumers. I can write a small tf-ref-updater that replaces the old sha with the new tag where safe.
alice: Short term plan: 1) Carmen opens shim hotfix PR in 30m. 2) Cut v1.2.5 with shim. 3) Run staging canary. 4) Open migration PRs for top 20 repos. Medium term: enforce CHANGELOG and compatibility matrix in module repos and add an automated check to PR template.
ben: Also noticed that the rename surfaced an implicit change in the KMS IAM config — `kms_config.requires_role` had implicit default false before; the new var combined with defaults produced null and caused the plan to attempt IAM changes. We need to set explicit defaults to avoid unintended role churn.
carmen: Good catch. I'll lock `default = false` for `requires_role` and re-run plan against staging gpupool.
dmitri: Suggested staging test command: ```bash
./ci/run-tfplan.sh --workspace=staging --modules=gpupool --diff-only > artifacts/gpupool_staging_plan.log
``` Save logs for auditing.
alice: Timeline: patch PR in 30m, release in ~1h, start canary in staging immediately after, hold 2 hours for observation, then roll to prod if no regressions.
ben: Prepare rollback playbook in case KMS or node join breaks: 1) revert module to previous tag, 2) apply with -target=module.gpupool, 3) monitor node autoscaler and KMS deny logs.
carmen: I'll paste the PR link when ready and add migration notes to our infra-runbook. Sorry for the churn — will follow deprecation cycle next time.
devops-bot: incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-137 assigned to @carmen: "TF module rename causing plan failures across GitOps pipelines".
dmitri: Long term, we should add an automated compatibility check that runs against a consumer matrix before merging module input changes — verify no consumer uses removed inputs.
alice: Agreed. @sre-ops can you shadow the canary for 2 hours post-rollout? Focus: GPU autoscaler, node join rates, and KMS deny logs.
sre-ops: Will do. I'll watch node provisioning metrics, join latency, and KMS error rate. Update in #incidents if anything spikes.
